title: CRP-dependent DNA anchoring and membrane sequestration define a dual mechanism for MtlR-mediated regulation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the full Zenodo deposit via its application programming interface: 35 files, all PNG images, 2.02 MB total, licence CC-BY-4.0; downloaded 'Figure 4B uncropped gel.png' (49,983 bytes, 590x472 pixels) and confirmed it is a photograph of a gel, not a table. No comma- or tab-separated file of any kind exists in the deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Contents of Supplementary Tables S1-S4 (strains/plasmids, primers, AlphaFold-Multimer interaction scores plus IIB-domain residue ranges for 391/383 species, AlphaFold3 predicted MtlR dimer helix angles for 391 species) are known only from the article text and methods. Europe PMC's supplementary-file endpoint timed out on two attempts, so the supplement itself is not retrievable; no numeric assay table is described anywhere in the paper.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record 21312595 is open (CC-BY-4.0); I listed all 35 files and downloaded one. No login needed. But the content is gel photographs only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the files: there is no label column anywhere. Every experimental readout (gel shift bands, surface-plasmon-resonance binding constants, enzyme-reporter activities, quantitative PCR ratios) exists only inside figure panels or raw gel images, so any target would have to be constructed by reading values off images. Scoring stopped here.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences are retrievable from UniProt/OrthoDB for the 391 species, so inputs would be obtainable; this is the only Part A item not blocking.

a4_units_stated.note: No units column exists because no measurement table exists; gel images carry no quantification. Units for binding constants appear in figure text only.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The largest tabular object described is 391 species (383 with the EIIMtl IIB domain) of predicted scores, plus a 256-protein in-silico screen. All are far under the ~1,500-row bar, and under 400 even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 2.02 MB of PNG images; a 391-row species table if it existed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is trivially laptop-friendly; that is the only easy part.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Zenodo file names map to the figure numbers as the deposit description claims; species counts (391 with MtlR+CRP, 383 with IIB domain) are internally consistent in the text. No count could be cross-checked against a data table.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL by circularity. The only numeric 'labels' in the paper are AlphaFold-Multimer v2.3 interface scores (ipTM, ipAE) and AlphaFold3 predicted dimer helix angles - outputs of other models, not measurements. Training on them would distil AlphaFold, with its accuracy as the ceiling.

existing_models.name: AlphaFold-Multimer v2.3 / AlphaFold3 (as used by this paper itself, via ColabFold)
existing_models.score_and_split: No benchmark reported here; used with an ipTM (predicted interface template-modelling score) cutoff of 0.6 to call interactions across 391 species
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Which lineages genuinely retain the MtlR-EIIMtl membrane-sequestration interaction; they validated only four species experimentally

existing_models.name: SPOC classifier / Predictomes (machine-learning filter separating true from false AlphaFold-Multimer interaction predictions)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors as separating true from false proteome-wide AlphaFold predictions; exact numbers not retrieved
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Raw AlphaFold confidence scores alone do not reliably separate real interactions from false positives

existing_models.name: PPIscreenML (structure-based protein-interaction screening on AlphaFold models)
existing_models.score_and_split: Described as outperforming raw AlphaFold confidence metrics for interaction screening; numbers not retrieved
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation of structure-based interaction screens beyond the training interaction classes

existing_models.name: RoseTTAFold2-Lite pathogen interactome screen (19 human bacterial pathogens, 78 million protein pairs, 1,923 confident complexes)
existing_models.score_and_split: 1,923 confident complexes from 78 million pairs; no held-out benchmark retrieved
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Distinguishing confident predictions from false positives at proteome scale

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model, small checkpoints run on a laptop CPU)
backbone.hardware: CPU only; 391 bacterial proteins embed in minutes

integration.partner_dataset: OrthoDB v12 plus UniProt and AlphaFold DB (predicted structures keyed by UniProt accession)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which bacterial lineages retain a non-canonical regulator that borrows another protein as its DNA-binding platform - unanswerable here because the only per-species values are AlphaFold outputs, with no measured interaction data to learn from.

controls.positive_control: The four species validated in vitro (Escherichia coli, Salmonella enterica, Vibrio cholerae, Vibrio splendidus) - four points, too few to control anything.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be possible on a 391-row AlphaFold-score table, but the labels are themselves model output, so a collapse test proves nothing about biology.
controls.external_validation: None: no second dataset measures MtlR-partner binding across species.

honest_claim_h3: At best a model could claim to reproduce AlphaFold-Multimer's own interface confidence scores for 391 Gammaproteobacteria from sequence, which is a statement about AlphaFold rather than about mannitol regulation.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use bacterial protein sequences to predict whether a sugar-sensing repressor binds its partner proteins across hundreds of species.
plain_idea.train_on: Protein sequences of MtlR (the mannitol-operon repressor), CRP (the cyclic-AMP receptor protein) and the membrane sugar transporter EIIMtl from the 391 Gammaproteobacteria species the paper analysed (383 for the transporter pair).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the repressor binds each partner. The only per-species answers in this paper are AlphaFold-Multimer confidence scores and AlphaFold3 predicted dimer geometry - computer predictions, not measurements; real binding was measured in the laboratory for just four species.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Bacterial-regulation groups would like a sequence rule for which species use this borrowed-DNA-binding strategy, but with four measured species and a few hundred model-generated scores the question cannot be answered from this paper.

more_or_better_data.why: 391 species of AlphaFold-derived scores and four experimentally tested pairs, against proteome-scale screens covering tens of millions of protein pairs (e.g. 78 million pairs across 19 bacterial pathogens).

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements of binding across species exist in the data, so per-prediction uncertainty could not be calibrated against anything measured.

models_beatable.why: The relevant models are AlphaFold-Multimer v2.3 and AlphaFold3 (2023-2024 structure predictors) plus recent machine-learning filters on their outputs; a sequence model trained on 391 of their own scores cannot beat them by construction.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: there is no measured ground truth to evaluate against, so no honest baseline comparison on a shared split is possible.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predicting, from bacterial protein sequence, whether the mannitol repressor MtlR forms a complex with CRP or with the membrane transporter EIIMtl across 391 Gammaproteobacteria. The only available per-species values are AlphaFold-Multimer and AlphaFold3 outputs, so the task reduces to distilling those predictors on a few hundred rows.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: 391 bacterial proteins through a small ESM-2 protein language model on CPU is minutes, and the whole Zenodo deposit is 2.02 MB (measured). The eight hours are for scraping species identifiers and sequences, since the supplementary table was unreachable.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows of measured (not predicted) binding values in the deposit: the answer is zero - 35 gel photographs, no table.

verdict_reason: Mechanistic bench paper; the only deposited data is 35 uncropped gel images (2.02 MB, verified), so A2 fails - no label column exists and any target would have to be read off figures. A5 and A8 also fail: the largest tabular object described is 391 species of AlphaFold-Multimer/AlphaFold3 scores, i.e. another model's output, under the row threshold.
